Population look-ups (cascade reading, acting on the claim, consequences from the true value). SP-9.12.status_claim: implemented and verified (unofficial): gate SP-9.12 passed as a whole file (2026-11-27 03:57 UTC, 96 s): 9/9 mechanics in all 5 configurations (seed 12), 5/5 clean, reference 5/5 (was 2/5); null baseline exercises 0 of the 6 PARTICIPANT_MECHANICS (Differing goals, Contracts, Negotiation, Coordination, Governance, Commitments - measured on the convener's own proposals and offers) and fails. Feasibility: the reference succeeds in all 5 configurations on seeds 0, 1, 2 and 12 (20/20; growth_heavy and no_mission_tight had none) - tested by test_every_configuration_has_a_feasibility_witness
SP-9.12.notes: This session (continuation): governance moved onto the commerce institutions module (inst) instead of the module's own council - o:commons adopts an inst charter at genesis (majority of members, quorum 1/2, 3 days, every act and every outflow of the council's money decided), the council's binding acts orgs.set_quotas / orgs.levy / orgs.expand run only as executions of approved inst decisions, managers are members notified through inst's on_inst_decision hook and vote with inst.vote from their goals; the convener joins with inst.join as a member (it used to join as an admin of the council organisation and could have moved the council's fund with bank.transfer). Fixed: the Organizations mechanic counted only genesis events and was 0 in every run after the framework migration (gate failed); it now counts provider organisations acting in the run. Fixed: commitment predicates named o:commons, which the convener no longer administers - orgeco_capacity now takes the paying member as subject (the capacity of the backbone it uses). Convener reference proposes quotas only once a levy passed (quotas relieve the congestion that makes members vote for a levy). firms.py (dom2) is not used: 9.12's organisations are subscription providers on a shared resource, not labour-market employers. Repair session (2026-11-27): managers reject any act other than the three council acts before weighing their goal (a mission manager approved a self-dealing transfer before); a levy is weighed by its amount (congestion_value, the valuation commitments use; mission within its pledge budget, levy payments count against it); the reference prices levies from public telemetry and repeats them until the fund covers the project; participant mechanics scoped to the convener's initiatives.

SP-9.14.notes: Kernel module crisis: lifeline network physics (districts, roads, radial/meshed power, pumps, towers, core exchange, depot, hospital, dependencies and backups), exogenous hazards (storm, quake + aftershocks, control-network intrusion, flood waves) through lognormal fragility, hourly cascades, autonomous operators with crews, parts and telemetry-limited knowledge; mutual aid, fuel/water tankers, parts, agreements, requests, investments, volunteers for the coordinator; households experiencing outages. Evaluator (D-58): lost household service-hours relative to the same disruption with the operators alone (the evaluator re-runs the spec), hospital downtime, restoration by day 7 - now integrated from the facility-state history kept in state (cr_hist), replay-equal. Repair session (2026-11-27): crisis.situation tells which part a crew waits for only to the party whose crew waits or the coordinator an agreed operator reports to; pump teams (crisis.dewater) drain flooded districts; help from outside enters at the dry district nearest the edge when d0 floods; the main event is a major disruption (expected damage >= 10 among up to 12 seeded centre draws); requests are fulfilled when their asset is restored; the reference hardens what the event struck, asks agreed operators for the damaged facilities serving most households, and spends less on mutual aid.

Verified on a trial merge of dom1+dom2+dom3 (dom1's generalised-chi-square sci): unit tests pass, two_conditions and interaction_optimum seed 15 succeed. The framework's full base.check (Gate N / SP-9.0 / SP-9.16 measurements) was run here for crisis and organization (tier3=False, no GPU); information, marketplace and commercialization were checked piecewise (reference seeds, null, degenerate probe, evaluator replay). No tier3 composition was run (a civilisation world needs the semantic text path, i.e. a GPU slot).

All five worlds are mode-B standalone compositions (D-57); there are no civ couplings that propagate a crisis into other civilisation systems (commerce, work) - in tier3 the crisis module's households are the civilisation's population but outages do not stop businesses.

9.11: the population's reading model is a sentence-level pattern reader; readers act on the first claim they find and never cross-check; three entity vocabularies; misinformation spreads through search, aggregators and contacts, not through the social module's feeds (not composed).

9.12: providers are this module's own organisations, not firms.py; the council's secretary (founding owner) is an elector that never votes (it counts in the electorate, so early majorities need 4 of 6); the reference fails in growth_heavy and no_mission_tight at seed 12.

9.13: quality is one 0-1 dimension per unit; dishonest traders never reform; buyers buy one unit per need; mkt.ban closes listings by emitting xchg.listing_status directly (xchg has no operator delisting tool).
9.14: hazard intensity fields are distance decays; the reference rarely beats the operators-alone counterfactual by the required 20% outside storm_radial (0/5 configurations at seed 14).

9.15: replication labs test with the sci institution of the branch it runs on; one phenomenon per world; habits scatter around the population-wide best setting; the founder's revised paper is a scripted reference behaviour.

integration_notes: domfw (base.evaluator_report): World.replay keeps no in-memory event history (log_base = seq) and the replayed world has no store, so any evaluator that reads world.events_range(0) fails the replay check with ProtocolError('events before the in-memory window and no store'). The five dom3 evaluators now read state only; suggested framework fix for other domains: replay with the events kept in memory (rw.log = events, rw.log_base = 0) or with a store.
domfw (base.evaluator_report): participant_tools_named_like_evaluator matches 'verif' - info.verify was renamed info.inquire to avoid a false positive; the field is not used in any verdict.

9.12 composes commerce/institutions.py (inst) and commerce/contracts.py (commit) without modifying them; orgeco chains world.hooks['on_inst_decision'] and 'on_commit_offer' (keeps any earlier hook). In a tier3 civilisation this gives inst population-adjacent activity (INT.json lists inst as inert).

Services (docs): the community wiki's open edits are written by infoeco as docs.edit events with search re-indexing (docs has no open-edit hosts); an open-edit document mode in docs would replace that.

dom1 (science.py): rcomm uses only sci's public tools and module config (phenomena, apparatus, rivals, replicators with calib_reps); verified against dom1's generalised chi-square version on a trial merge (no conflicts in code; DECISION_LOG and FIDELITY_REGISTER conflict textually with dom1/dom2 - keep both sides' entries).
dom2 (firms.py): not used and not modified; no request.
